messages.subject: ggvis 0.1
parts:
[email in response to the ggvis announcement, that Hadley asked me to
post tot he group for further reference]

That is very cool, congratulations! I've cloned it and played with it
a bit. Do you want bug reports right away or are you still working on
stuff that you know is broken?

A couple comments:

- bring us back the grey background! ;) I guess style is not the main
issue at this very early stage. But style was what initially sold me
(and probably others) to ggplot, so it is something to keep in mind.

- I don't understand the need for the ~ in props
ggvis() + layer_point(props(x=~foo, y=~bar))
I thought it was to differentiate between mapping and setting
aesthetics but setting seems to require := . So I would have
understood:
ggvis() + layer_point(props(x=foo, y=bar, size:=2))
or
ggvis() + layer_point(props(x~foo, y~bar, size=2))
but do not understand
ggvis() + layer_point(props(x=~foo, y=~bar, size:=2))
In terms of the "elegance" of the code, this last solution does not
seem ideal to me. I would personally prefer the second one because it
is the most meaningful, but understand it might not be feasible
technically. But the first one still looks OK.
It might seem very minor given that you are probably buried in vastly
more complex problems but it will eventually have its importance (when
writing ggvis code every day) and won't be changeable later, so I
thought I would mention it.

PS: one last question: I noticed Hadley uses Sublime Text. I use
TextMate. RStudio is becoming nicer and nicer but I cannot get my
fingers to ditch TextMate. Using ggvis outside of RStudio opens a new
browser tab every time which is a bit annoying. How do you work with
ggvis outside of RStudio?

Thanks again, a lot, for your great work and thank your bosses for me,
to pay you to bring us such awesomeness for free ;)

> It might seem very minor given that you are probably buried in vastly

> thought I would mention it.

We thought really really hard about this, and have about 10 different
variations we tried. In the end, we liked this solution because it's
only slightly more verbose that ggplot2, but is more explicitly, which
makes quite a few new things possible. We'll be striving to convince
you of this as we flush out the documentation for properties.

> PS: one last question: I noticed Hadley uses Sublime Text. I use
> TextMate. RStudio is becoming nicer and nicer but I cannot get my
> fingers to ditch TextMate. Using ggvis outside of RStudio opens a new
> browser tab every time which is a bit annoying. How do you work with
> ggvis outside of RStudio?

We are open to suggestions. Unfortunately ggvis is fundamentally web
based so it has to open in a browser. It might be possible to use a
specific browser's API to re-open the graphic in the same tab, but it
seems like this is going to be hard to do across browsers.

Hadley

I have no idea what that really entails but a nice solution would be
to have a custom R graphic device.
This is not entirely appropriate:
http://www.omegahat.org/RGraphicsDevice/overview.html
but mentions things like:
http://rforge.net/canvas/
which seems dead but the general idea was here.

Actually, reading those resources, it seems that a "device" means that
you implement the drawing primitives (line, rect, circle etc.). What
you would need is really just a renderer. Maybe simple things like
this:
http://www.macdevcenter.com/pub/a/mac/2004/01/23/webkit.html
can help. Basically, you need a webview (based on webkit?) that loads
one file at a time(and possibly keep history). How hard cant it be...
right? ;)
